newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: GOVT RESPONDS TO WALLIS REPORT
The Federal Government has lifted the blanket ban on the mergers between the four major banks and two major life insurance companies, in its response to the Wallis report into the financial system.
It's also lifted the ban on a foreign takeover of any of the four big banks.
But the Government is keeping the power of veto over both areas.
The Treasurer, Peter Costello, says there'll be no mergers between the four banks at this stage.
The Wallis report has recommended the establishment of two regulatory authorities, one for prudential supervision and another for market conduct.
Mr Costello says the report's recommendations also provides the opportunity for greater choice and lower prices for consumers.
The Australian Consumers' Association says the Treasurer's recommendation against the big four banks merging is good news.
But the Association's, Peter Kell, says he's worried consumer protection will be weaker under a proposed new super-regulator than under the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
KERNOT URGES COLSTON TO RESIGN
Australian Democrats leader, Cheryl Kernot, says public confidence in the Senate has been eroded as a result of the Mal Colston affair.
Senator Kernot has urged Senator Colston to resign from the Senate before it resumes in five weeks'time.
The Government's referred allegations about Senator Colston's travel entitlements to the Federal Police and has called on the Independent to stand down as Deputy Senate President.
On the Gold Coast today, Senator Kernot said Mal Colston should resign from the Senate immediately to prevent it from being brought into further disrepute.
BUILDING SOCIETIES WELCOME WALLIS
Australia's building societies believe the Wallis Report into the financial system will provide smaller organisations opportunities to effectively compete against the banks.
The building societies say that by putting them under a single regulator with the banks, they'll all be on the same footing.
Chairman of the Association of Permanent Building Societies, Paul Lahiff, says Wallis also underlines the part smaller organisations play in offering a real competitive alternative to customers.
TEACHERS' FEDERATION BACKS GAY STUDENT'S TEACHERS
The Teachers' Federation has expressed its support for the staff of western Sydney's Cranebrook High School, which is being sued by a former student.
Christopher Tsakalos is suing the school and other students claiming he was the subject of homosexual vilification.
The Federation's executive says the school, its staff and its community have been criticised without substantiation.
The Federation says education rather than litigation is a more appropriate way of dealing with homophobia, and says staff of the school have been denied natural justice.
LAND COUNCIL OPPOSES ARMY UPGRADING ABORIGINAL SERVICES
The Cape York Land Council says Aboriginal people themselves, and not the Army, should be given the job of upgrading water and sewerage systems in Aboriginal communities.
The Council's Policy Advisor, David Byrne, says a scheme by the Howard Government to use the Army to help upgrade infrastructure in Aboriginal communities is continuing stupid policies of the past.

Mr Byrne says Aboriginal people in the communities should be given training and employment to put in the services and maintain them afterwards, rather than having the Army provide a short term solution.
SHINE DONATES MEMORABILLIA TO SYDNEY PLANET HOLLYWOOD
Sydney's Planet Hollywood has become one of just two of the restaurants in the world to have received memorabillia from the Australian film -- "Shine".
Among the memorabilia are early press clippings about David Helfgott, sheet music, and plaster-cast hands of Rachmaninoff.
Planet Hollywood's Lisa Kable says the New York restaurant has also received a raincoat worn by Geoffrey Rush in the film.
METEORS SIGHTED OVER NORTHERN TERRITORY

A research officer at Canberra's Mount Stromlo Observatory says reports of bright lights over the Territory yesterday are the latest sightings of several meteors entering the atmosphere. Callers to Darwin talkback radio and the observatory say the light was moving at high speed, leaving a trail from it's tail.
Vince Ford from the Observatory believes they've seen a bo-lide, similar to other balls of fire spotted in other parts of the country recently.
Mr Ford says usually about a dozen of these bolides are reported every year, and it's unusual to have three sightings in two weeks.
